what: does a TimesFM-3-architecture model gain from more pretraining data? Two runs with the same model and recipe, differing only in the corpus
model: TimesFM3Torch (timesfm 3.0.2 code), d_model 768, 14 layers, 12 heads, no variate attention, 50,918,592 parameters, random init
recipe: global batch 1024 windows, context 2048, pinball loss on 9 quantiles per 64-step output patch, AdamW 5e-4, 2,000 warm-up steps, cosine over 150,000 steps, 10% KernelSynth, uniform-over-series sampling; 4 H100s per run, run concurrently; stopped at about 75,000 steps once the answer was clear
verifier: tests/test.sh path (sealed, cohort-wise, uid isolation), all 97 configs, 326,490 instances, about 15 min of inference each
reading: With 41 GB the validation skill peaked at 25,000 steps and fell while the training loss kept falling (overfitting); with 273 GB it kept improving to 45,000 steps. On test, A at its best checkpoint matches the 41.8M starter (0.206 vs 0.207) at about a tenth of the compute, and B exceeds it (0.217). Both runs drifted after their peaks with the learning rate still high, which motivated source-balanced sampling for the shipped baseline (baseline/timesfm3-50m).
